body:
I would instead expose the offsets on `CowData` and use them here.
That would make the coupling direct and protect against drift explicitly.
Or do you have a reason to prefer re-deriving them here?

No particular reason to duplicating these here, other than they're defined as private members of a templated class so they're inaccessible, and this patch is coming from a consoles fork where minimizing changes outside platform code is the priority, so that assumption tends to leak out when I upstream patches, even modified ones like this. I can move the cowdata definitions out of the class and make them accessible, that would certainly make this a lot safer.
The core change is warranted for me since it just reflect our decision to expose the offsets 👍
Oooof, good catch. And I looked through this code a million times already!
Made the cowdata definitions public so we can use them here :+1:

`godot_plugins_initialize_fn *&r_initialize_fn` is a ref to a pointer to a function pointer.
It should be a ref to a function pointer instead:

```suggestion
bool initialize_coreclr_and_godot_plugins(godot_plugins_initialize_fn &r_initialize_fn, godotsharp_marshaling_init_fn &r_marshaling_init_fn) {
```

The reason is that your proposed signature is one indirection too many, which I think causes the coreclr path to incorrectly assign later, which would lead to a crash on launch. 

(you could also fix this by using `(void *&)(*r_marshaling_init_fn)` below instead, but I think that would be a confusing representation of what you're trying to do).

I recommend changing all init function signatures to use the "ref to function pointer" form.

Ah, good catch, I tested all the codepaths but I must have then made that change and not run the coreclr path afterwards. Some init functions call other functions that take refs to pointers to function pointers, while other init functions call other functions that take one indirection less. All of this duplicated-yet-slightly-different init code makes it complicated to properly harden these codepaths, let me run all of these codepaths on all the platforms again and see how best to handle this.
I think Core was fine with making these public on `cowdata.h` so we can reference them directly and avoid these going out of sync over time.

I tried, but I ended up not doing that because those definitions in cowdata.h rely on typedefs that are inside classes, and making it all visible and properly usable would require a lot more disruptive changes and header dependencies. It was surprisingly hard to access those cleanly. It would require a bit of a larger refactor in cowdata than what I was comfortable with for this PR (it should be done though, these are important implementation details that need to be exposed to all languages and consumers, but maybe not here).
Okay, we can keep it like this too. CI will fail anyway if there's a mismatch (hopefully).
These are `uint` on the C# side. I think that's different from `size_t`?

Yup, it is narrower on the C# than it is on the C++ side, the marshaling will clamp the values going from native to managed to match the narrower C# size. Which won't have any effects in practice because these values are always smaller than INT32_MAX, but I'll fix the C# side to match, both sides should match.

@Ivorforce I'll put a big pin on my todo list to expose the relevant bits from cowdata so they're accessible from anywhere, it's important, so hopefully this doesn't have to sit like this for too long. I also want to backport this to 4.6+, so it's handy that this is more contained like this right now.
`ulong` isn't the same as `size_t` in 32 bit i think. The new code is also incorrect.
